name: Liar’s Dice
intro: A short path through Liar’s Dice: bids, wild ones and challenges, then the one-in-three rule for judging a bid and when to call “Liar!”.

units.name: How Liar’s Dice works
units.blurb: Bidding, wild ones and calling Liar.

lessons.title: Bids and wild ones
lessons.summary: In Liar’s Dice you bid on how many dice show one number across the whole table, with ones wild. Learn to count your dice and raise a bid.
lessons.wrap: More dice, or the same number of a higher face. Next: a quick rules check.

steps.text:
Everyone rolls five dice in secret. Players take turns bidding on how many dice of one number are on the whole table, not just in their own cup.

Ones are wild: a 1 counts as any number. Bids are on 2s to 6s.

steps.prompt: Tap every one of your dice that counts towards it.
steps.wrong: Count the 4s, and don’t forget that a 1 counts too.
steps.done: Three of yours count: two 4s and the wild 1.

steps.text: Each bid must be higher than the last: more dice, or the same number of dice with a higher face.
steps.prompt: The last bid was three 5s. Which of these is a legal raise?
steps.explain: Three 6s: same number of dice, higher face. Four of anything would work too.

steps.text: Instead of raising, you can call “Liar!”. All the dice are shown. If the bid was true, the caller loses a die; if not, the bidder does.
steps.prompt: You call Liar on five 3s. The table shows four 3s and one 1. Who loses a die?
steps.explain: Four 3s plus the wild 1 make five, so the bid was true and you lose a die. The last player with dice wins.

units.name: Rules check
units.blurb: Five questions on the rules. Pass to unlock the strategy.

lessons.title: Liar’s Dice rules check
lessons.summary: Test your Liar’s Dice rules: counting wild ones, legal raises, what happens after a challenge, and how the game is won.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now for the odds.

steps.prompt: Tap each of your dice that counts towards five 6s.
steps.wrong: The 6s count, and so does the 1.

steps.prompt: The last bid was four 6s. Which is a legal raise?
steps.explain: After 6s, the only way up is more dice: five of any face.

steps.prompt: Which dice count towards a bid of 4s?
You bid six 5s and someone calls Liar. There are only five. Who loses a die?
steps.explain: The bid was false, so the bidder loses a die.

steps.prompt: How do you win the game?
options: Be the last player with dice left
steps.explain: Every lost challenge costs a die. The last player with dice wins.

units.name: Odds and calling
units.blurb: The one-in-three rule and when to call.

lessons.title: Bid odds: one in three
lessons.summary: With ones wild, a third of the dice you can’t see should count for any face. Use the one-in-three rule to judge every bid in Liar’s Dice.
lessons.wrap: Your dice, plus a third of the rest. Next: when to call.

steps.text:
Any die you can’t see has a 1 in 3 chance of counting for a given face: it could be that face or a wild 1.

So a fair guess for any face is your own matching dice, plus a third of everyone else’s.

steps.prompt: Tap your dice that would count in a bid on 5s.

steps.text: There are 20 dice on the table: your 5 and 15 you can’t see.
steps.prompt: About how many 5s are on the whole table?
steps.explain: Your 3, plus about a third of 15, which is 5. About 8 in total.

steps.text: Bid on what you hold: your own dice make the bid more likely to be true. Now it’s just you and one opponent, 10 dice in all.
steps.explain: You hold three 6s (two 6s and a wild 1), and the 5 hidden dice should add one or two more, so about four or five in all. Two 6s is safe and leaves room to raise. Raising slowly passes the pressure on.

lessons.title: When to call Liar
lessons.summary: Call Liar when a bid is well above what the one-in-three rule expects, and raise when it’s close. Practise the call on real Liar’s Dice hands.
lessons.wrap: Work out the expected count, then call or raise. Try it against the computer.

position.label: The bid: six 4s, 10 dice on the table

steps.text: Before you call, count what the bidder needs.
steps.prompt: You have no 4s and no 1s. Should you call Liar on six 4s?
steps.explain: None of your dice count, so all six would have to be among the other five dice. It can’t be true: call.

position.label: The bid: five 4s, 15 dice on the table

steps.prompt: Should you call Liar on five 4s?
steps.explain: You have three, and the 10 hidden dice should add about three more: about six in all. Five is likely true, so raise instead.

position.label: The bid: seven 3s, 20 dice on the table

steps.prompt: You hold three that count. Is seven 3s close or far from what you’d expect?
steps.explain: Three, plus a third of 15, is about 8. Seven is likely true. If the bid were 11 or 12, you’d call. Being slightly wrong costs a die either way, so when it’s close, make a small raise you can back up.
